articles.title: Israeli strike on vehicle distributing food aid in Gaza kills three
articles.text:
Israeli strike on vehicle distributing food aid in Gaza kills three | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
Save
Share
A Palestinian man holds the blood-stained logbook of a van that was transporting food aid to displaced people after it was targeted by Israeli forces, killing three people, in Al-Sina'a Street in the Tel al-Hawa area, west of Gaza City on November 21, 2026 [AFP]
By Al Jazeera Staff
Published On 21 Nov 202621 Nov 2026
Israeli attacks in Gaza have killed at least four Palestinians in violation of last year’s “ceasefire”, as winter flooding deepens the humanitarian crisis in the enclave.
At least three people were killed when a van delivering food aid to displaced people was struck by an Israeli drone on Saturday in the Tal al-Hawa neighbourhood of Gaza City.
Recommended Stories list of 3 items
list 1 of 3 Gaza’s displaced children celebrate World Children’s Day
list 2 of 3 Can Israel’s opposition bloc stay united against Netanyahu?
list 3 of 3 Demolition notices for buildings in Hebron provoke fear among Palestiniansend of list
A witness told the Reuters news agency that papers inside the van bore the logo of World Central Kitchen, an aid organisation that distributes food in Gaza, but the organisation said the vehicle was not affiliated with it.
“It’s a bus that distributes food and drink to the poor, to the people in tents, to the displaced,” said Abu Zein al-Daya, a displaced Gaza resident who witnessed the attack. “It was just about to stop to distribute the food and drinks to children, and then it was hit by a missile. The target is anyone who is giving the people food.”
In a separate attack, a Palestinian man was killed by Israeli gunfire in the Halawa displacement camp, east of northern Gaza’s Jabalia refugee camp.
Al Jazeera’s Ibrahim al-Khalili, reporting from Gaza City, said the man was then taken to al-Shifa Hospital.
Earlier on Saturday, he said, an Israeli attack targeted a young man on an electric bicycle in al-Mawasi, in Khan Younis in southern Gaza. There, three people were injured and taken to Nasser Medical Complex.
“The ceasefire has yet to deliver a change for the people in Gaza,” al-Khalili said. “Israeli attacks and gunfire have been part of the grim reality for the people in Gaza.”
Advertisement
Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza has continued despite a so-called “ceasefire”, which came into force last October. More than 1,600 Palestinians have been killed since then.
Blood stains the doors of a van that was transporting food rations to displaced people after it was targeted on Saturday [AFP]
Settler violence in the West Bank
The ongoing attacks on the enclave coincide with a surge in pogroms carried out by Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank.
Late on Friday, Hamza Masoud Salim Abdo, 42, was shot dead by security guards from an illegal Israeli settlement near the village of Dura al-Qari, north of Ramallah.
The Palestinian Health Ministry said his body was being withheld by Israeli authorities. Another Palestinian man was detained during the incident.
Reporting from Ramallah in the West Bank, Al Jazeera’s Nour Odeh said settlers have been carrying out attacks with “impunity”.
“Less than 3 percent of Israeli attacks that are investigated lead to a partial or full conviction by Israeli authorities. Also, the number of settler attacks reported to Israeli authorities is very, very low because Palestinians are often detained, questioned or harassed for filing reports against violent settlers,” Odeh reported.
The violence inflicted on Palestinians in the West Bank has been condemned by Israeli allies, including the United Kingdom. Critics say Western leaders have not supported their rhetoric with sufficient action.
Earlier this month, an Al Jazeera investigation found that the UK had awarded $14.4m in new public contracts to firms with links to illegal Israeli settlements in the West Bank, despite recently announcing a ban on importing goods from such settlements.
The British government has also sanctioned companies involved in settlement expansion.
‘Uncertain’ days ahead
Winter weather has compounded the humanitarian crisis in Gaza, with the World Food Programme (WFP) warning earlier this week that Palestinians have been forced to burn rubbish to cook their food.
“Now even the rubbish is wet,” warned Shaun Hughes, WFP’s country director for Palestine.
The International Organization for Migration (IOM) has said that more than 100,000 tents in Egypt cannot be delivered to Gaza due to strict conditions imposed by Israel, including limits on the diameter of the tents’ central poles.
“Usually anything under 38 millimetres is OK; anything above, it’s usually deemed as not acceptable,” Hughes explained.
“It is not a statement of dual use; it is just that this tent at this time is not allowed to enter Gaza … We don’t get the specifics,” said Karl Baker, head of the IOM’s Gaza programme.
Advertisement
Al Jazeera’s al-Khalili, reporting from Gaza, said: “The coming days are uncertain, and the lack of basic necessities looms.”
Gaza’s Health Ministry reported on Saturday that 1,671 people had been killed since the “ceasefire” came into effect in October 2025. Al-Khalili said Israel has committed more than 600 ceasefire violations since then.
Meanwhile, 74,736 Palestinians have been killed since Israel launched its genocidal war on Gaza three years ago.

articles.title: Russian crew evacuating ship hit by drones off coast of Finland
articles.text:
Russian crew evacuating ship hit by drones off coast of Finland | Russia-Ukraine war News | Al Jazeera
Save
Share
The Russian cargo vessel Sparta II is shown on fire off the southern coast of Finland after being struck by two drones on Saturday [Finnish Border Guard photo]
By David Mac Dougall and Reuters
Published On 21 Nov 202621 Nov 2026
The crew of a Russian ship in the Gulf of Finland, hit by drones likely launched by Ukraine, is being evacuated into life rafts and a rescue boat.
Finnish authorities say the Sparta II has links to Russia’s armed forces and has drifted into territorial waters off Finland’s southern coast.
Recommended Stories list of 3 items
list 1 of 3 Why is Ukraine attacking Russian warships in the Baltic Sea amid talks?
list 2 of 3 Russia complains of ‘new Iron Curtain’ as Estonia shuts its borders
list 3 of 3 Russian missiles hit Poland: What happened, and could NATO respond?end of list
“There is a fire on board the ship. The situation does not pose a danger to maritime traffic or people. A restricted area has been set up around the site to ensure safety,” the Finnish Border Guard said in a statement, adding that it is in “close international cooperation” with neighbouring countries, including contact with Russia’s maritime rescue authorities.
How the attack unfolded
On Saturday morning, Finland’s Ministry of Defence said its forces detected a drone attack on a Russian vessel in international waters, with initial reports saying the ship had sustained damage. Finnish Border Guard units were dispatched to the scene, and a photograph taken by a Finnish patrol plane showed flames and thick smoke coming from the rear of the ship.
The attack happened west of Gogland Island, off the coast of the Finnish town of Loviisa, and Finland quickly implemented temporary air and sea traffic restrictions in the eastern part of the gulf.
A Russian helicopter has since violated Finnish airspace, venturing more than 4km into Finnish territory.
“The suspected airspace violation is possibly related to rescue or tracking operations of a damaged cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland. The Defence Forces and the Border Guard are handling the situation in cooperation with other authorities,” said Minister of Defence Antti Hakkanen.
Advertisement
By Saturday afternoon the Finnish Defence Forces said the strike was likely carried out by Ukraine. Earlier, Finland’s Prime Minister Petteri Orpo wrote on X that “war is spilling over into our immediate vicinity. The Finnish authorities are handling the situation in the Gulf of Finland, where a drone strike has hit a Russian merchant vessel. Ukraine has the right to fight back against the aggressor.”
What do we know about Sparta II?
Finland’s Border Guard said the Sparta II is known to have links to Russia’s armed forces. The roll-on-roll-off ship was built in the year 2000 and sails under a Russian flag, according to the vesselfinder.com website.
“At the moment, ⁠⁠⁠⁠there is no confirmed information about ⁠⁠⁠⁠what cargo is on ⁠⁠⁠⁠board, but ⁠⁠⁠⁠it cannot be ruled out that there ‌‌‌‌is military materiel on board,” Iljin said.
Alexander Drozdenko, governor of Russia’s Leningrad region, said damage to the ship had yet to be fully assessed.
“Three nautical miles from the Russian Federation’s border, a cargo vessel bound for Kaliningrad was attacked by two drones,” he wrote on the messaging app Max.
Kaliningrad’s Governor Alexey Besprozvannykh said supplies to the Russian exclave were not at risk.
One of the major risks of attacking any vessel is environmental damage if it leaks or sinks, a scenario that Baltic Sea nations treat with high importance. That risk is “further amplified by the poor state of some of the so-called ‘Shadow Fleet’ tankers” that Russia operates, according to Robin Haggblom, senior adviser for Risk Intelligence and an expert in Finnish maritime issues.
“Actions to prevent environmental damage has also been emphasised in Finnish Border Guard communication regarding this event. Luckily in this case, we don’t yet have ice coverage in the Gulf of Finland, which would impact any oil spill recovery efforts that may be needed,” Haggblom told Al Jazeera.
The vessel was bound for the Russian enclave of Kaliningrad [Al Jazeera]
Crowded shipping lanes
The narrow and shallow waters of the Baltic Sea are some of the most crowded shipping lanes in the world. The Helsinki to Tallinn ferry route had 7.5m passenger crossings last year. Other passenger routes link Baltic ports and capital cities, and cargo vessels and military shipping contribute to the total number of vessels in the relatively small body of water.
So if Ukraine is using drones – maritime or aerial – to hit Russian ships, could there be any risks to civilian vessels?
“There obviously always is a risk of collateral damage. However, so far Ukraine does seem to be taking a number of steps to minimise the risks involved, with the Sparta II for example apparently having been identified and hit a handful of kilometres from Russian waters,” added expert Haggblom.
Advertisement
Earlier this month, Finland’s military said it had detected a strike on a Russian warship in the Gulf of Finland, which Ukraine took credit for. Helsinki later said it had raised concerns with Kyiv about strikes in the area.
“It is the same with the strike on the Russian corvette earlier, where it is reported the Ukrainians were able to pick it out and target that specific vessel among perhaps a dozen other ships. There are also unconfirmed indications that Sparta II was targeted specifically, and not just as a general Russia-associated merchant vessel,” Häggblom added.
Ukraine and Russia have attacked each other’s shipping throughout the war, mostly in the Black Sea.
Advertisement

articles.title: India’s opposition stages protests against Meta over account removals
articles.text:
India’s opposition stages protests against Meta over account removals | Censorship News | Al Jazeera
Save
Share
Indian Youth Congress members hold signs during a protest against the suspension of their party leaders' accounts, outside a Meta office building in Mumbai, Maharashtra, India, November 20, 2026, in this picture screengrab from a social media video [Indian Youth Congress/via Reuters]
By Al Jazeera Staff, Anadolu and Reuters
Published On 21 Nov 202621 Nov 2026
The youth wing of India’s main opposition Congress party has staged protests outside Meta offices in three cities, demanding that the United States technology company restore the Instagram accounts of its leaders.
The protests took place in Hyderabad, Mumbai and Gurugram, near New Delhi, on Friday and led to clashes with police and security guards, according to footage released by the Indian Youth Congress on Saturday.
Recommended Stories list of 4 items
list 1 of 4 ‘Manipulated’: Kenya to US midterms, Indian bots help campaigns sway votes
list 2 of 4 The Global South’s digital future must not belong to Bezos and Musk
list 3 of 4 Will India’s ‘Cockroach’ movement force Modi’s BJP to rethink its politics?
list 4 of 4 How Ambani’s Jio became India’s second-largest companyend of list
In Hyderabad, protesters entered the building that houses Meta’s offices and clashed with police. In Mumbai, protesters spray-painted slogans on the walls outside, and in Gurugram they held banners reading “restore Youth Congress accounts”.
The party has alleged that on November 19, Meta illegally withheld the Instagram accounts of the youth wing’s president and the party official overseeing the wing on orders from the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
In a statement accompanied by videos of the protests, the Congress youth wing said, “If Meta wants to do business in India, it must respect the Indian Constitution, not surrender to arbitrary BJP government orders.”
It had also warned Meta on X that it would “storm your offices across the country and stage protests” unless the accounts were restored.
Manu Jain, who runs the group’s social media, told the Reuters news agency on Saturday that two accounts were restored after Friday’s protests, but thousands of other accounts of journalists, creators and influencers critical of the government are still restricted.
The youth wing issued a seven-day “ultimatum” to the technology giant, urging it to lift all “restrictions on opposition voices, journalists and creators”.
Advertisement
It asked how many Indian accounts were withheld on government orders in the past six months, and how many remain blocked. It also asked Meta to explain what it called the automated blocking of posts that mention Congress leader Rahul Gandhi or criticise Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the BJP.
On Saturday, the protesters also posted a video of workers putting up a banner in central Delhi that mocked Meta’s chief executive, Mark Zuckerberg, as “Mark BJPberg” – suggesting that Meta favours Modi’s party.
Meta has yet to issue a statement on the matter.
Police action and BJP response
Police registered a complaint against four Youth Congress leaders in Mumbai and detained some protesters, Dainik Jagran English reported.
Pradeep Bhandari, a spokesperson for the ruling BJP, accused the protesters of vandalising Meta’s Hyderabad office and “flaunting it on social media”.
India is Meta’s biggest market by users.
In February, the government ordered platforms to remove unlawful content within three hours of notice, down from 36 hours. The government issued nearly 195,000 blocking orders to Instagram, Facebook and YouTube between March and July, the Indian Express reported.
Meta restricted more than 5.4 million posts or accounts in India under local laws in the first half of 2026, up from about 70,000 in the whole of 2025, according to its disclosures. It said most were cases in which it was “obligated to proactively restrict content” under local law.

articles.title: Who is El Chapo Isidro, the alleged cartel boss arrested in Mexico?
articles.text:
Who is El Chapo Isidro, the alleged cartel boss arrested in Mexico? | Crime News | Al Jazeera
Save
Share
This handout image of a poster obtained November 21, 2026 from the FBI's Most Wanted Fugitive list shows an undated photo of Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores, also known as 'Chapo Isidro' [AFP]
By Al Jazeera Staff and The Associated Press
Published On 21 Nov 202621 Nov 2026
Mexican special forces have arrested Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores, an alleged cartel leader known as “Chapo Isidro”, who is on the FBI’s Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list, Mexico’s defence ministry said.
Meza-Flores was detained along with two other men on Friday night in Guasave, in the northwestern state of Sinaloa.
Recommended Stories list of 4 items
list 1 of 4 Ecuador’s president denies existence of US military base
list 2 of 4 Mexico captures FBI-wanted cartel boss in military raid
list 3 of 4 What we know about Mexican drug cartel leaders still at large
list 4 of 4 Is the US arming Mexican cartels?end of list
The arrest comes as US President Donald Trump has been pressing Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum to do more to combat drug cartels and said on Friday that Washington was working with Sheinbaum “because the cartels are running Mexico.”
“I told her that,” he said. “And we can’t let the cartels run Mexico. They’re our neighbour.”
Who is Chapo Isidro and what is he accused of?
Despite the similar nickname, Meza-Flores is not related to Joaquin “El Chapo” Guzman, the jailed former leader of the Sinaloa Cartel.
Mexican authorities say Meza-Flores leads the Beltran Leyva criminal organisation and is an ally of the Mayos faction of the Sinaloa Cartel. The Mexican Secretariat of National Defence said he was wanted in Mexico on an arrest warrant for organised crime and drug offences and is subject to an extradition order to the United States.
US prosecutors first indicted Meza-Flores in 2012. In a 2019 indictment, they accused him of conspiring to manufacture and distribute cocaine, heroin, methamphetamine and marijuana for the US market between 2005 and 2019. He also faces a firearms charge.
The FBI added him to its Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list in February 2025, and the US Department of State offered up to $5m for information leading to his arrest and conviction.
Advertisement
“Known as El Chapo Isidro, he’s accused of spending the last 20 years flooding the US with fentanyl, cocaine, heroin, and other deadly drugs, first as an independent drug trafficker and later as the head of the Meza-Flores cartel,” said then-acting FBI Director Brian Driscoll in announcing his addition to the list.
He also said Meza-Flores and his organisation were accused of kidnapping, extortion, torture and murder.
How was Chapo Isidro arrested?
Mexico’s defence ministry said the operation followed coordination between Mexican and US intelligence agencies and involved special forces from Mexico’s National Guard and army.
Troops used “stealth and surprise” to establish a security perimeter around a house in Guasave and came under attack with gunfire and explosives before entering and arresting three men, the ministry said.
It identified the other two as German N, known as “Serafin”, the group’s alleged second-in-command, and Jose N, who they identified as a financial operator. The three men were flown to Mexico City and handed over to prosecutors.
Sinaloa’s public security agency urged residents to stay indoors, avoid the area, and stay off the roads, as federal personnel had been attacked in Guasave.
The defence ministry said roadblocks were reported in four areas of Sinaloa after the arrests and that security forces were sent to reopen roads.
Videos from Guasave showed people fleeing gunfire at a baseball game, as well as cars and petrol stations on fire, The Associated Press news agency reported.
Mexico’s security secretary, Omar Garcia Harfuch, said on Saturday that troops would remain in Sinaloa to protect residents.
“These detentions are an important step toward restoring peace in Sinaloa,” he wrote on X.
Advertisement

articles.title: Riemann hypothesis: Has the world’s most famous maths problem been cracked?
articles.text:
Riemann hypothesis: Has the world’s most famous maths problem been cracked? | Science and Technology News | Al Jazeera
Save
Share
Georg Friedrich Bernhard Riemann (1826-1866), German mathematician [Undated Portrait/Getty Images]
By Heba Habib
Published On 21 Nov 202621 Nov 2026
A mathematician from the tech giant Anthropic claims to have proven one of the world’s most famous – and most elusive – maths problems with the help of AI.
Levent Alpoge wrote on his website on Friday: “I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis.”
Recommended Stories list of 3 items
list 1 of 3 California files lawsuit against OpenAI alleging lack of proper safeguards
list 2 of 3 AI models abandon climate facts to please users, UNESCO report finds
list 3 of 3 China’s DeepSeek unveils latest models a year after upending global techend of list
If his claim holds up, the proof he says he has would settle a question that has defeated mathematicians for 167 years. Independent experts are now trying to verify it, but so far no human has read through the entire argument.
Here is what we know.
What is the Riemann hypothesis?
First proposed by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann in 1859, the hypothesis concerns the distribution of prime numbers and is widely regarded as the most important open question in pure mathematics.
Prime numbers are whole numbers which can be divided only by one and themselves, such as 2, 3, 5 and 7. They appear to be scattered along the number line with no obvious pattern but the Riemann hypothesis proposes that their overall distribution actually follows a deep, hidden order – just one that humans have yet to identify.
“The Riemann hypothesis is the most famous and important unsolved problem in mathematics,” Abhishek Saha, professor of mathematics at Queen Mary University of London, told Al Jazeera.
“The patterns of the primes are encoded in a mathematical object called the Riemann zeta function, introduced by Bernhard Riemann in 1859.”
It is one of the seven Clay Mathematics Institute Millennium Prize Problems, each carrying a $1m award.
Advertisement
What has the Anthropic mathematician claimed?
Alpoge, a member of the company’s technical staff, made the announcement on Friday in a four-page explanation posted on his website. He said the proof he has found covers the generalised Riemann hypothesis, which extends the original conjecture to a broader family of mathematical functions.
He did not publish a conventional paper. Alpoge released the argument in Lean, a programming language and proof assistant that checks reasoning step by step. He was open about how much of the work was Claude’s, writing that “Claude far outpaced me near the finish line”.
Kevin Buzzard, professor of pure mathematics at Imperial College London, said nobody yet understands what the proof actually shows.
“At the minute, we don’t even know why the theorem is true,” he told Al Jazeera. “It’s 17 million lines of Lean code, and this might correspond to tens of thousands of pages of mathematics. We don’t even yet know how much of this mathematics is new ideas, how much of it is just sort of standard stuff the machine just had to develop.
“At the minute, the proof is just millions of lines of gobbledygook written in a strange programming language,” he said. “And right now, as we speak, there’s people all over the world who are translating parts of this programming language back into English.”
He expects answers to come fairly soon, however. “Experience shows you that you give the humans the Lean code, and within a week or two, they have a much better understanding of what’s actually going on in this code,” he said.
Why is the Riemann hypothesis so important?
“The implications of this hypothesis extend across large parts of mathematics, and hundreds of other mathematical results have been proved assuming this hypothesis is true,” Saha said. “A proof would settle a question that has occupied some of the greatest mathematical minds for over 160 years.”
Buzzard said the result also matters beyond pure mathematics, including for internet security.
“We know there are some algorithms that we run where they’re very quick, but we don’t actually know for sure if they work,” he said. “They seem to work, and we know that if the generalised Riemann hypothesis is true, then they do work.”
He said cryptographers had long worked on the assumption that the Riemann hypothesis is true. “In practice, people do tend to assume that the Riemann hypothesis is true because it’s a viable hypothesis to assume, because there’s so much evidence that it’s true,” he said. “But we can sleep slightly safer in our beds at night because it is true.”
Advertisement
Buzzard said the result stands out among recent AI breakthroughs in mathematics. He compared it with the Navier-Stokes problem, another Millennium Prize problem, which OpenAI said an unreleased AI model had solved in September. “That one doesn’t really have any applications at all,” he said, calling it “just of theoretical interest”. “Whereas the Riemann hypothesis has applications to neighbouring fields.
“It’s a very hard problem, but it’s definitely not the hardest problem in mathematics,” he said, pointing to even stronger versions such as the “extended Riemann hypothesis and the grand Riemann hypothesis”.
“The Riemann hypothesis is just, in some sense, at the foot of a mountain,” he said. “We’re beginning our trek up the mountain with this theorem.”
Why has it remained so elusive for so long?
“The problem is relatively simple to state, but extraordinarily difficult to prove,” Saha said. “Mathematicians have developed vast amounts of sophisticated theory in their attempts to solve it, but none of the techniques developed over the past 167 years has been sufficient. The direct methods have all been tried, and none of them come close to resolving it.
“Until very recently, most mathematicians, myself included, believed that a proof would require substantial new

articles.title: Could Iran reverse its stated policy of a civil-only nuclear programme?
articles.text:
Could Iran reverse its stated policy of a civil-only nuclear programme? | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
Save
Share
Iranian missiles and banners showing portraits of Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei are displayed in a military exhibition at Baharestan Square, in Tehran on September 28 [Vahid Salemi/AP Photo]
By Stephen Quillen
Published On 21 Nov 202621 Nov 2026
Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has said the country’s stockpile of enriched uranium will be used according to its needs, “however they are defined”, as he spoke about possible changes to Iran’s longstanding nuclear doctrine.
Araghchi’s comments during an interview with Iranian media on Saturday have increased speculation that Iran may be moving away from its policy of limiting its nuclear programme to civilian purposes amid its conflict with the United States.
Recommended Stories list of 3 items
list 1 of 3 Is Iran plotting a ‘dirty bomb’ attack in the US? What we know
list 2 of 3 US Navy chief says Iran war has put ‘strain’ on maritime forces
list 3 of 3 Trump claims Iran is developing bioweapons: Is there any evidence?end of list
The future of Iran’s nuclear programme has become a major sticking point in efforts to end the war, with Washington insisting that it must have guarantees that Iran will never develop a nuclear weapon before it will agree to a full ceasefire.
So, is Iran’s nuclear policy changing, and what could that mean for the conflict?
What is Iran’s official nuclear policy?
Iran has consistently maintained that its nuclear programme is for peaceful purposes only, such as for electricity generation, medical research and agriculture.
This policy has been underlined by a decades-old religious decree, or fatwa, issued by the late Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, banning the development of nuclear weapons.
However, Iran has also insisted it has the right to enrich uranium for these purposes under the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons (NPT), which it joined in 1970. It has called this right “non-negotiable”.
What have Araghchi and other officials said?
In an interview with Iran’s state-run IRNA news agency on Saturday, Araghchi reiterated that Iran’s stockpile of enriched material would remain inside the country.
Advertisement
The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) estimated in 2025 – before Israel launched strikes on Iran in June that year – that Iran had about 440 kilogrammes (970 pounds) of uranium enriched to about 60 percent. This is short of the 90 percent required for making nuclear weapons, but is the level at which it becomes much quicker to reach 90 percent. It is also far beyond the roughly 3 percent needed for power generation.
This material, Araghchi said during his interview, would “be used according to our needs however those needs are defined”.
Araghchi also made reference to an ongoing debate among lawmakers and officials in Iran about altering its nuclear doctrine, and said people on both sides of that debate have “strong arguments”.
“This is a major strategic debate, and there is nothing wrong with examining it seriously because it directly concerns national interests and security,” Araghchi said, adding that those in favour of reform argue Iran’s current approach of no nuclear weapons has “failed to protect” the country’s nuclear facilities, which have come under attack from US and Israeli forces both last year and this year.
However, Araghchi acknowledged that any official change to the policy would have “far-reaching consequences”.
“For now, our doctrine has not changed, and our official position remains the same,” he said.
Other Iranian officials have also spoken about a potential review of the country’s nuclear doctrine. Earlier this month, security chief Mohsen Rezaei said “there is a discussion on whether we want to continue to follow the previous nuclear doctrine in the event of a new war breaking out”, though he also stressed that Tehran has not yet made any change.
On November 12, Iran’s Assembly of Experts, the body that appoints the supreme leader, said reviewing “the country’s defence doctrine and establishing the necessary deterrence have become unavoidable necessities”.
Ali Fathollah-Nejad, a German-Iranian political scientist who directs the Center for Middle East and Global Order (CMEG), told Al Jazeera the move by the Assembly of Experts “appears to mark the first time a governing institution has endorsed this position”.
Why do the US and Israel think Iran is developing nuclear weapons?
Besides being a signatory to the NPT in 1970, Iran also initially complied with a nuclear agreement it struck with the US and other global powers in 2015 – the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA), which required it to limit uranium enrichment to very low levels and undergo inspections.
Advertisement
But after Washington pulled out of the deal in 2018 under the first administration of US President Donald Trump, Tehran eventually went back to intensifying its nuclear programme and abandoned restrictions imposed by the deal.
In June 2025, the IAEA’s board of governors declared Iran was no longer complying with its commitment to international nuclear safeguards. Tehran rejected that report and accused the IAEA of giving a pretext for US and Israeli attacks targeting Iranian nuclear facilities, including Fordow, Natanz and Isfahan, just days later during the 12-day war.
In March of this year, IAEA chief Rafael Grossi said at least 200kg (440lbs) of Iran’s enriched material was believed to have survived the US-Israeli attacks and was likely buried underground in or near the Isfahan nuclear facility site.
Grossi has since said the agency cannot verify the amount or location of Iran’s enriched material due to a lack of access.
The IAEA has called Iran’s enrichment level “a matter of serious concern”, while the US has pointed to it as evidence that Iran is pursuing nuclear weapons despite its official policy.

articles.title: US midterms 2026: What happens before the new Congress takes office?
articles.text:
US midterms 2026: What happens before the new Congress takes office? | US Midterm Elections 2026 News | Al Jazeera
US Midterm Elections 2026
Save
Share
The dome of the US Capitol in Washington, DC, on November 17, 2026 [Nathan Howard/Reuters]
By Al Jazeera Staff
Published On 21 Nov 202621 Nov 2026
The United States midterm elections are over, and the Democrats have won control of both houses of Congress. However, they do not take power until January.
Election officials are still certifying results, while the newly elected lawmakers are preparing to take office, and the outgoing Congress is continuing its legislative work.

So what happens between now and January, and what will change as the 120th Congress takes office?
What has happened so far?
After the elections, officials have been finalising the results and completing the certification process, which varies by state.
On November 9, the existing Congress returned to Washington for what is known as the “lame-duck” session.
A lame-duck session occurs when Congress meets after an election but before the new Congress takes office.
This means the Republicans still have the majority in both chambers of Congress and can continue passing legislation until the new Congress takes office in January.
November-December: New lawmakers prepare to take office
During this time, newly elected members start preparing to take office in January.
They attend orientation sessions in Washington, hire staff, and learn more about how Congress operates day-to-day.
Political parties also choose their leaders in the House of Representatives and the Senate. The party controlling each chamber selects the majority leader, while the other party selects the minority leader. The House will also vote on a speaker, who leads the House leadership.
The Republican Party has already re-elected John Thune as its Senate leader, entering the final two years of Donald Trump’s presidency.
Advertisement
The election on the Democratic side, however, is shaping up to be more of a fight.
Among Democrats, Senator Chris Van Hollen of Maryland is challenging Senator and current Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer of New York to be Senate majority leader, with a vote scheduled for December 1.
Speaking on Al Jazeera’s This Is America, Democratic strategist Roger Fisk suggested that the differences between the two candidates may be more about their methods than their political goals.
“I think the difference would probably come in the how rather than the what,” Fisk said.
Republican strategist Doug Heye said the leadership debate reflects wider questions facing both parties after the midterms.
“Both parties have somewhat of an identity crisis,” he said, referring to the Republicans’ losses and the future of the party but also the divisions in the Democratic Party between moderate Democrats and more progressive ones.
(Al Jazeera)
December 11: A government funding deadline
One of the biggest challenges of the current Congress is a December 11 deadline to approve government funding.
Congress passed a temporary spending bill, known as a continuing resolution, to keep the federal agencies functioning without approving a full-year budget.
But before the measure expires, Congress must approve another bill to keep the government funded.
If lawmakers do not reach a deal, part of the federal government could face a shutdown.
Speaking to Al Jazeera, Heye suggested a temporary funding extension could push negotiations into February, by which time Democrats will control both chambers.
“So that would probably go through February,” he said, referring to a possible continuing resolution.
Heye also said the federal debt ceiling is another challenge for the new Congress.
“These are two things that never come up on the campaign trail, but it can be very important to tell us about the next two years,” he added.
(Al Jazeera)
December 17-18: Congress wraps up
The current Congress is expected to finalise its legislative work before the Christmas holidays.
The House’s final sitting day is planned for December 17 and the Senate’s for December 18.
But lawmakers could remain in Washington longer if major issues remain unresolved.
Even if lawmakers finish their work earlier, the 119th Congress’s term does not officially end until January 3.
January 3, 2027: The new Congress takes power
The 120th Congress starts its term at noon (17:00 GMT) on January 3, 2027.
But January 3 falls on a Sunday, and Congress could pass a law setting a different date for the first meeting.
Advertisement
When the new House convenes, lawmakers must elect a Speaker before being sworn in. Newly elected senators will also take their oaths.
With Democrats controlling both chambers, they will gain authority over congressional committees, legislative priorities and investigations into the administration of President Donald Trump.
“You’re going to have in the House and the Senate something called committee chairs, and they’re all going to be Democrats, and they’re all going to have subpoena power,” Heye told Al Jazeera.
However, he warned that congressional investigations could complicate negotiations between Democrats and the White House.
What changes politically in January?
Trump will remain president after the midterms, but he will face a Congress controlled by Democrats in both chambers.
This means his administration will have to negotiate with the Democrats to pass legislation, while a Democrat-led Senate will control the confirmation process for presidential nominees.
Democrats will also be able to launch congressional investigations and hold hearings looking at the president’s actions and the actions of those in his inner circle and administration.
